summary.headline: Azad Engineering Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR187.8 crore (+31.6% YoY) with EBITDA margin at 37.5%, while PAT was held down by depreciation, finance cost and lower treasury income.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR187.8 crore, up 31.6% YoY and 10.1% QoQ, with EBITDA up 37.1% to INR70.4 crore at a 37.5% margin. PAT was INR30.8 crore (16.4% margin), dragged by depreciation that doubled to INR21.8 crore, finance cost of INR12.2 crore and treasury income falling to INR4.7 crore from INR12.7 crore. Management says the setup phase is complete: all six customer-dedicated facilities are commissioned and throughput begins Q3 FY27, with revenue ramping from Q4 and full ramp-up by H1 FY28. Working capital remains the key pressure, with H1 operating cash flow negative at INR45.8 crore, and management is pursuing OEM advances and bill discounting to fund it.

segments.name: Energy and oil & gas
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue INR290 crore (about 81% of revenue), up 28.5% YoY; Q2 revenue stated as INR152 crore, up 30.02% YoY. Dedicated Baker Hughes oil & gas facility expected to add growth from Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Aerospace and defence
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue INR60.4 crore (about 17% of revenue), up 28.3% YoY; Q2 revenue stated as INR31.7 crore, up 31.6% YoY. Management said last year's aerospace revenue was INR100 crore.

segments.name: Domestic (India)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 domestic revenue more than 2.5x to INR43 crore, now 12% of business (from 6%), helped by BHEL indigenisation work. Exports were 88% of Q2 revenue.

guidance_outlook: Throughput from new capacity begins Q3 FY27; revenue ramps from Q4 FY27; all plants fully ramped up by Q2 FY28 (management also said H1 FY28 in the call).
Installed capacity supports an annual revenue run rate of over INR1,300 crore by end FY28, more than double FY26 revenue; management called this a conservative floor.
Long-term annual growth guidance reiterated at over 25%.
Confident of meeting long-term EBITDA margin guidance in the coming quarter or so; depreciation to step up further in Q3 and Q4 FY27 before stabilising.
Export share expected to remain about 85% of sales.
Cash generation expected to turn positive around Q4 FY27, with Q1 FY28 cited as more comfortable for cash flow.
capex_capacity: All six customer-dedicated facilities at Tuniki Bollaram are commissioned, totalling 44,800 sq m for MHI, GE Vernova, Siemens Energy and Baker Hughes; two GE Vernova lean facilities were inaugurated in September 2026.

H1 FY27 capitalisation of INR251 crore of new assets; H1 capex INR139.3 crore funded by INR80.8 crore QIP money and INR28.6 crore term loan and internal funds. Fixed assets incl. CWIP at INR1,169 crore.
QIP of INR700 crore: INR621.8 crore used, INR78.2 crore held in fixed deposits for remaining capex.
Mangampet land earmarked for Phase II; management says it is well covered for future capacity.

Rolls-Royce dedicated capex made in 2024; two engine programmes in qualification with production to start on these lines. Management did not give a fresh capex figure for FY29 onwards; a QIP may be used when growth needs it.
demand_pricing: Management described an order book of over INR6,500 crore but corrected the term, saying it is a rolling set of contracts covering the next five to seven years, not a formal order backlog.
BHEL approved as long-term source for gas turbine airfoils under a two-year rate contract of about INR52.68 crore. Baker Hughes supply agreement with Nuovo Pignone extended to 2030.

MHI single-source nozzle vane / hot section contract for eight years has started; aero-engine airfoil work with Rolls-Royce, Pratt & Whitney and Safran expected to start delivering from next fiscal year.
Wallet share with existing customers is under 2% (single-digit); management sees large growth from existing customers.
Management expects energy to fall to about 55-60% of revenue by FY30-31 with aerospace and defence making up the rest.
Price concession on OEM advances was about 1%, per management, and not material.

qa_highlights.question: How will aerospace contracts move from development to production and what revenue acceleration follows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said buildings, machines and foundations are ready, spindles are running, and throughput started with about two to three weeks of delay. Revenue is expected to rise from Q3 and ramp in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: When will cash burn peak and free cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supplies start at the end of Q3 and in Q4, with cash expected to flow out of the company by Q4 FY27 end; Q1 FY28 was cited as a comfortable point. Bill discounting lines with ICICI Bank and DP World are available from Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is ARR of INR1,300 crore a floor, and does INR1,800-1,900 crore of total capacity hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR1,300 crore is the bare minimum and throughput now exceeds it; it did not confirm the INR1,800-1,900 crore framing and said it would update the range next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How many Rolls-Royce, Pratt & Whitney and Safran qualifications are in process, and when does aero revenue start?
qa_highlights.answer: Rolls-Royce is in qualification for two engine programmes, with Pratt & Whitney Canada and Safran next. Management said the first qualification batch is almost complete and it will announce first deliveries soon; there is no production revenue from Rolls-Royce yet.

qa_highlights.question: What drives growth beyond FY29 and is there new capex planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new capex for FY29 onwards will be planned once current engine programmes qualify and customers open further volumes; it may use a QIP when required. Visibility on current contracts is said to cover the next five years.

qa_highlights.question: How does headcount scale and does automation reduce labour intensity?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost spiked ahead of revenue as skilled staff were hired. Management expects manpower cost to fall as revenue ramps over one to two quarters and aims to rely more on automation and ERP, with the cycle repeating over four to six quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Did OEM advances come with margin concessions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the discount on advances is about 1%, not material, and that OEMs were asked to support working capital because the company is funding capex and working capital.

risks_watch: Working capital: H1 FY27 operating cash flow negative INR45.8 crore; inventory up INR98 crore to INR425 crore and receivables up INR92 crore to INR402 crore. Watch for cash turning positive around Q4 FY27 as guided.

Ramp-up timing: throughput from new capacity begins Q3 FY27 with revenue ramp from Q4 and full ramp-up by H1 FY28 (also stated as Q2 FY28); management acknowledged a two-to-three week delay in the spindles' start.
Aerospace conversion: first Rolls-Royce qualification batch described as almost complete with no production revenue yet; Pratt & Whitney Canada and Safran qualifications still in process.

Capacity framing: management did not confirm the INR1,800-1,900 crore total capacity figure from an analyst and said it would update the range next quarter; the INR6,500 crore figure is a rolling set of contracts, not an order backlog.

Margin and cost base: depreciation expected to step up further in Q3 and Q4 FY27; finance cost rising with working capital loans; bill discounting lines with ICICI Bank and DP World from Q4 FY27 add finance cost; long-term EBITDA margin guidance expected to be met in the coming quarter or so.
Post-FY29 growth: no fresh capex figure given beyond FY29; management said new capex will follow once current engine programmes qualify, possibly funded by QIP. Export share expected near 85%.
key_quotes: Three months on, every single we track has strengthened.
For Azad, the question is not demand, it's how quickly we convert capacity into revenue and that is the key message for this quarter.
This is not order backlog. Just wanted to bring that slide to one side.
summary.management_tone: Management is confident on demand, capacity and margins, but cautious and often vague on timing: it repeatedly deferred specifics on order book, capacity range, aero qualifications and the cash inflection to later quarters. It was evasive on the engine programme and the post-FY29 capex plan, citing customer restrictions.

adds.what: Six customer-dedicated facilities at Tuniki Bollaram (44,800 sq m) for MHI, GE Vernova, Siemens Energy and Baker Hughes, all commissioned

growth.why: Management reiterates long-term growth of over 25% and an annual revenue run rate above INR1,300 crore by end FY28; the six commissioned dedicated facilities (INR251 crore capitalised in H1) and QIP-funded capex back it, with throughput from Q3 FY27 and ramp from Q4, though the INR6,500 crore "order book" was corrected to rolling contracts, so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management is confident of meeting long-term EBITDA margin guidance (32%-35%) in the coming quarter or so, but Q2 margin already at 37.5% and depreciation steps up further in Q3-Q4 FY27 while bill discounting and finance costs add pressure, so the reported margin path is mixed.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: All six customer-dedicated facilities at Tuniki Bollaram (44,800 sq m) are already commissioned, INR251 crore capitalised in H1 FY27, and throughput begins Q3 FY27 with ramp from Q4 and full ramp by H1 FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management reiterates long-term growth above 25% and a run rate above INR1,300 crore by end FY28 (vs FY26 revenue of roughly half that), with H1 FY27 revenue up 29.3% YoY and throughput starting Q3 FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Fixed assets incl. CWIP at INR1,169 crore and Mangampet land covers Phase II, but no fresh capex figure was given beyond FY29 and management said new capex will follow qualification, possibly via QIP; QIP balance of INR78.2 crore remains for current capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 FY27 revenue of INR358.3 crore grew 29.3% vs guidance of over 25%, and management called the INR1,300 crore run rate a conservative floor, though it deferred any capacity range update to next quarter.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Ramp started with a two-to-three week spindle delay, cash flow is negative (H1 operating cash flow -INR45.8 crore) with working capital rising, and aerospace production revenue depends on Rolls-Royce, Pratt & Whitney and Safran qualifications still in progress.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Two Rolls-Royce engine programmes are in qualification with first deliveries to be announced soon, and aero-engine airfoil work with Rolls-Royce, Pratt & Whitney and Safran expected to deliver from next fiscal year.

rows.label: Cash flow turns positive
rows.why: Management guided cash to turn positive around Q4 FY27 (Q1 FY28 more comfortable) after H1 operating cash flow of -INR45.8 crore, with OEM advances (about 1% discount) and bill discounting lines with ICICI Bank and DP World available from Q4 FY27; inventory INR425 crore and receivables INR402 crore remain high.

rows.label: Dedicated MHI nozzle vane contract ramp
rows.why: MHI single-source eight-year nozzle vane / hot section contract has started, and BHEL two-year rate contract of about INR52.68 crore is in place, with Baker Hughes dedicated facility adding growth from Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Net debt rising with capex
rows.why: Net debt is INR423.8 crore (1.6x annualised EBITDA) with finance cost up to INR12.2 crore from INR6.4 crore a year ago, and working capital lines and bill discounting add to borrowing before cash inflects.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the six dedicated facilities and margins, but cautious and vague on timing of the order book, capacity range, aero qualifications and cash inflection, and evasive on engine programmes and post-FY29 capex; analysts pressed on the INR1,800-1,900 crore capacity frami

oneOffs.what: Other income fell to INR4.7 cr from INR12.7 cr a year ago, a treasury drop that depresses PAT growth but is not in revenue growth

quality.why: Q2 revenue rose 31.6% YoY to INR187.8 cr with no acquisition or one-off revenue item cited; the brief gives no volume percentage, but the growth is tied to new capacity and customer programmes, while the depressed treasury income weighs on PAT rather than revenue growth.
